steps.tx: Blood and mucus passed per rectum resembling fruit jelly is **red currant jelly stool**. It signals bowel wall congestion in intussusception and appears relatively late. Its absence never excludes the diagnosis in a colicky infant. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Red currant jelly stool signals congested bowel in intussusception but appears relatively late.

steps.tx: Pushing the telescoped bowel back with air or fluid pressure is **hydrostatic reduction**. Pneumatic reduction under imaging succeeds in most stable infants without peritonitis. Failure, perforation or shock mandates immediate surgery. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: Hydrostatic or pneumatic reduction pushes telescoped bowel back in most stable infants.

steps.tx: Absence of ganglion cells in the distal bowel causing functional obstruction is **Hirschsprung disease**. The aganglionic segment stays contracted, so stool accumulates above it. Delayed passage of meconium beyond forty eight hours is an early clue. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Hirschsprung disease lacks ganglion cells in distal bowel and delays meconium passage.

steps.tx: The junction between narrow aganglionic and dilated normal bowel is the **transition zone**. Contrast enema shows this calibre change, usually in the rectosigmoid region. Biopsy remains necessary because imaging can mislead. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: The transition zone shows calibre change on enema, though biopsy remains necessary.

steps.tx: Definitive treatment pulls ganglionated bowel down to the anus, called a **pull through operation**. A preliminary colostomy may be needed in sick or late presenting children. Bowel function afterwards is usually good with time. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Pull through operations bring ganglionated bowel to the anus for Hirschsprung disease.

steps.tx: Life threatening enterocolitis complicating Hirschsprung disease is **Hirschsprung enterocolitis**. Explosive foul diarrhoea, distension and sepsis develop rapidly. It can occur before or after surgery and needs urgent resuscitation and washouts. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Hirschsprung enterocolitis causes explosive diarrhoea and sepsis needing urgent resuscitation.

steps.tx: Most intussusceptions in infants have no structural lead point and are called **idiopathic**. In older children, a polyp, Meckel diverticulum or lymphoma may lead the telescoping. Recurrence after enema reduction happens in about one in ten. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Infant intussusception is usually idiopathic, while older children may have a lead point.

steps.tx: A sausage shaped mass palpable in the right abdomen with emptiness below it is **Dance sign** territory. The right iliac fossa feels empty because the caecum has moved upward. This supports intussusception on examination. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: An empty right iliac fossa with a sausage mass supports intussusception on examination.

steps.tx: Children with peritonitis or perforation bypass enema attempts and go to **immediate surgery**. At operation, gentle squeezing reduces viable bowel, while dead segments are resected. Delay converts a reducible problem into bowel loss. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Peritonitis or perforation means immediate surgery, where dead bowel is resected.
